messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet users,

I am trying to model dynamic network processes which consists of
observations of network structure at three points in time on the same node
set using STERGM in R. But since the network is large and sparse I am
having some problems. I have no experience before on using stergm.

My question is  how to effectively use control.stergm in large and sparse
networks?

I used a very simple model and again R got a problem and closed without
showing any warnings.

formation= ~edges ,
dissolution = ~edges,
control = control.stergm(
MCMC.init.maxedges=20000,
MCMC.init.maxchanges=20000,
CMLE.MCMC.burnin = 1024*16,
CMLE.MCMC.interval = 1024,
EGMME.main.method=c("Gradient-Descent"),

EGMME.MCMC.burnin.max=100000,

messages.subject: [statnet_help] TERGM
messages.body_plain:
Shiran,

There is no detailed book or online course at this point.  But one of the 
benefits of the STERGM approach is that each component of the model, 
formation and dissolution, is an ERGM.  So to interpret the dissolution 
model coefficients, you can use the conditional logit interpretation, 
as you would for a regular ERGM (refer to the ERGM tutorial).  The only 
thing to keep in mind is that the dissolution model is parameterized in 
terms of *persistence* of partnerships -- so positive coefficient values 
imply that the term increases the conditional odds of a partnership 
persisting.  As always, you need to keep in mind the other terms in the 
model when you interpret any individual terms.

If you have more specific questions, let us know.

best,
Martina

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Random bipartite graphs
messages.body_plain:
Yes, you can do this in statnet.

One approach:

net <- network.initialize(n=50, bipartite=25, directed=FALSE)
net %v% 'type' <- c(rep(1,25), rep(2,25))
target.edges = 100
fit <- ergm(net~edges, target.stats = target.edges)
bip.sim <- simulate(fit, nsim=5)
plot(bip.sim[[1]], vertex.col='type')

note that the "target.stats" argument should be a vector giving the value 
of the network statistics in the model (in the same order as they are 
listed in the model).  in this case, there's only one statistic, edges, so 
only one target.stat.

you can modify this to specify the density in obvious ways.

hth,
mm

messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiran,

This is precisely the kind of scenario where bootstrapped MPLE is both 
unbiased and fast. Try the btergm function in the xergm package, which 
has the same syntax as the ergm function in statnet and takes care of 
node composition change automatically. If you'd like to read up on the 
bootstrap approach, I recommend this paper: 
http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.physa.2011.10.018. If you need help setting 
it up, I may be able to assist with troubleshooting.

180 nodes is about the size of the international system of states, and I 
have previously run analyses on international conflicts or alliances 
(with similar densities as you are describing) over more than 50 years 
without any problem and in less than an hour. xergm implements TERGMs, 
not STERGMs, but ultimately this is just a matter of data 
transformation. The btergm function can also run in parallel on your 64 
cores via the MPI protocol, so estimation should be super fast. Only a 
fraction of your RAM should be required; I have run my models and done 
goodness-of-fit assessment with only 16 GB of RAM and that was no problem.

That said, perhaps others can comment on why the STERGM gets stuck. I 
would assume that the STERGM is estimated by MCMC-MLE, and MCMC-MLE is 
just prohibitively slow when the normalizing constant in the denominator 
of the ERGM equation gets blown up by the 50 time points.

Best,
Philip

side-by-side, take a look at this: http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/jopart/muu043.

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Statnet for cellular network
messages.body_plain:
Dear statnet group,

First, I would like to congratulate you for this fantastic package I found
it very interesting. I'm a postdoctoral researcher about cellular
technologies (5G). Since I have been using R from last three years, I want
to use it for my future research. I wasn't sure to find a package to
simulate a network and then I have found your collection of packages. Thus,
I would like to use this package to simulate my research on cellular
networks. My research aims to reduce the connection delay when a user goes
from a small cell (base station) to another while he/she is connected to
avoid service failure (e.g. making a call). My scenario is formed by three
different nodes: Macro base stations, small cells and users. The macro
cells are connected to one or more small cells. the small cells are not
connected between them, the communication between small base stations must
be through the macro base station. Macro base stations and small base
stations are static nodes. The users are dynamic, they should move randomly
along the network and they are connected to the small base stations. Is it
possible to simulate such network?

Thank you for your help. Do not hesitate to contact me for further
information.

Sincerely,

Dr. Ra?l Parada
